chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who comes to me, so I buy goods for him from the people and guarantee payment on his behalf. Then he comes to me with the dirhams, so I take them and withhold them from their owner, and I take the good-quality dirhams and give the inferior ones in their place. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he guarantees payment, perhaps the burden becomes heavy upon him, so he hurries to pay before I ask for it, and he withholds [payment] after receiving [the goods]; there is no objection to this.'

key_terms.أَضْمَنُ: I guarantee / I act as surety
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: There is no objection / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pay off a debt with lower quality currency or goods when acting as a guarantor?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the permissibility of a guarantor (*kafeel*) who buys goods on credit for another, addressing the concern of *riba* (usury) in the exchange of currency or goods. Imam al-Rida (AS) rules it permissible (*la ba'sa*) because the guarantor’s retention of funds or use of inferior currency is driven by practical commercial urgency or common practice, rather than a fixed interest charge on the loan itself. This distinction is crucial in Shia jurisprudence for differentiating between a simple guarantee (*kafala*) and interest-bearing loans.
